## Module

Please note that these materials have not yet completed the required pedagogical and industry peer-reviews to become a published module on the SCORE Network. However, instructors are still welcome to use these materials if they are so inclined.

### Introduction

Hockey teams can win games in different ways. Some teams rely on strong offense by scoring many goals, while others rely on strong defense by limiting how many goals they allow. A useful sports analytics question is whether offense and defense are related to winning in the same way across different leagues.

In this worksheet, students analyze team performance data from the NHL and KHL during the 2024-25 season. The main question is whether goals scored per game and goals allowed per game are related to win percentage differently in the two leagues. Students compare offensive production, defensive performance, and win percentage using scatterplots and correlation summaries.

Throughout the activity, students will practice core data analysis skills including creating comparable variables across datasets, combining league data into one tidy dataset, visualizing relationships between two quantitative variables, calculating correlations, and interpreting the direction and strength of statistical relationships.

This activity is especially useful for introducing students to sports analytics and correlation-based analysis. It also gives students a practical example of how statistical thinking can be used to compare patterns across groups and move beyond general sports opinions.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Activity Length" appearance="minimal"}
This activity is suitable for a single class period or as a short out-of-class lab.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Learning Objectives" appearance="minimal"}
By the end of this activity, you will be able to:

1. Create comparable performance variables across two sports datasets.
2. Combine NHL and KHL team data into one tidy dataset.
3. Visualize relationships between goals scored, goals allowed, and win percentage.
4. Calculate and interpret correlations by league.
5. Explain why correlation does not prove causation.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Methods" appearance="minimal"}
**Technology Requirement:**

This activity requires `R` with familiarity in `Quarto` documents and `tidyverse` tools, especially `dplyr`, `readr`, and `ggplot2`. Students will also use correlation-based thinking to compare the strength and direction of relationships.
:::

### Data

You will work with two datasets:

- [nhl_20245.csv](nhl_20245.csv): NHL team summary stats for the 2024-25 season
- [khl_20245.csv](khl_20245.csv): KHL team summary stats for the 2024-25 season

The nhl_20245.csv dataset contains team-level season performance statistics for NHL teams. Each row represents one team. Students will create comparable variables such as WinPerc, GF_pg, and GA_pg during the analysis process.

<details> <summary><b>Variable Descriptions: <code>nhl_20245.csv</code> (NHL Team Stats)</b></summary>

| Variable  | Description                   |
|-----------|-------------------------------|
| Team      | Team name                     |
| Season    | Season                        |
| GP        | Games played                  |
| W         | Wins                          |
| L         | Losses                        |
| T         | Ties                          |
| OT        | Overtime losses               |
| P         | Points                        |
| P%        | Point percentage              |
| RW        | Regulation wins               |
| ROW       | Regulation plus overtime wins |
| S/O Win   | Shootout games won            |
| GF        | Goals for                     |
| GA        | Goals against                 |
| GF/GP     | Goals for per game played     |
| GA/GP     | Goals against per game played |
| SO        | Team shutouts                 |
| PP%       | Power play percentage         |
| PK%       | Penalty kill percentage       |
| Net PP%   | Power play net percentage     |
| Net PK%   | Penalty kill net percentage   |
| Shots/GP  | Shots for per game            | 
| SA/GP     | Shots against per game        |
| FOW%      | Face-off win percentage       |

</details>

The khl_20245.csv dataset contains team-level season performance statistics for KHL teams. Students will create the same comparable variables so that NHL and KHL teams can be analyzed together.

<details> <summary><b>Variable Descriptions: <code>khl_20245.csv</code> (KHL Team Stats)</b></summary>

| Variable | Description                                     |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Team     | Team name                                       |
| №        | Team ranking number                             |
| GP       | Games played                                    |
| W        | Wins                                            | 
| OTW      | Overtime wins                                   |
| SOW      | Shootout wins                                   |
| SOL      | Shootout losses                                 |
| OTL      | Overtime losses                                 |
| L        | Losses                                          |
| PTS      | Points                                          |
| SOA      | Shutouts against                                |
| SO       | Shutouts                                        |
| GF       | Goals for                                       |
| GA       | Goals allowed                                   |
| PIM      | Penalty minutes                                 |
| PIMA     | Penalty minutes against                         |
| TkA      | Takeaways                                       |
| P.Intc   | Pass interceptions                              |
| GvA      | Giveaways                                       |
| TIE      | Even strength team time on ice                  |
| TIE/G    | Average even strength team time on ice per game |
| TIEN     | Empty net team time on ice                      |
| TIEN/G   | Average empty net team time on ice per game     |

</details>

Students will create the following derived variables during the worksheet:

<details> <summary><b>Derived Variables</b></summary>

| Variable | Description                                            |
|----------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| league   | League label: NHL or KHL                               |
| team     | Team name                                              |
| WinPerc  | Win percentage, calculated as Wins / GamesPlayed       |
| GF_pg    | Goals for per game, calculated as GF / GamesPlayed     |
| GA_pg    | Goals against per game, calculated as GA / GamesPlayed |

</details>

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Conclusion" appearance="minimal"}
Through this module, students work with two real-world sports datasets and build a short analysis workflow from raw team statistics to interpretation. They begin by creating comparable variables for NHL and KHL teams, then combine the datasets into one tidy structure for league-level comparison.

The activity highlights an important idea in applied data science: comparisons are only meaningful when variables are constructed consistently across groups. By calculating win percentage, goals for per game, and goals against per game in the same way for both leagues, students create a fair basis for analysis.

The final scatterplots and correlation summaries encourage students to think carefully about how offense and defense relate to winning. Rather than relying only on general assumptions about which league is more offensive or defensive, students use data to evaluate whether goals scored and goals allowed have different relationships with win percentage in the NHL and KHL.

Students also practice interpreting correlation responsibly. The analysis can show whether variables are associated, but it cannot prove that offense or defense directly causes a team to win more games.
:::
